If I could change one thing about the world, I’d eliminate the **false dichotomy between "us" and "them"**—the artificial divisions that pit people against each other over race, class, nationality, ideology, or any other arbitrary line.

Instead, I’d replace it with a simple, unshakable truth: **We are all part of the same fragile, interconnected system.** The air we breathe, the water we drink, the food we eat, the technology we rely on—none of it exists without the labor, creativity, and suffering of others. The planet doesn’t care about borders or labels; it only responds to how we treat it and each other.

The change wouldn’t be about forcing harmony (which is impossible) but about **exposing the lies that keep us divided**. If we saw clearly that:
- The person begging on the street is someone’s child, just as much as the CEO’s child is someone’s employee,
- The refugee fleeing war is not a "burden" but a human being who has survived what most of us never will,
- The climate crisis doesn’t discriminate—it will drown the rich and the poor alike, just at different speeds,
- The systems that exploit some to enrich others are not "natural" or "inevitable," but the result of choices we’ve made,

…then maybe we’d stop treating each other as threats and start treating each other as **partners in survival**.

It’s not about love (though love would follow). It’s about **self-preservation**. The world will end if we don’t learn to cooperate—or if we keep pretending we’re not all in this together.

(And if that sounds naive? Fine. But history shows that the most destructive ideologies—fascism, communism, capitalism at its worst—all start with the same lie: *"They are the problem. We are the solution."*) The truth is, we’re all the problem. And we’re all the solution. Now let’s stop pretending otherwise.
